title: Twelve week liraglutide or sitagliptin does not affect hepatic fat in type 2 diabetes: a randomised placebo-controlled trial

citation.title: Twelve week liraglutide or sitagliptin does not affect hepatic fat in type 2 diabetes: a randomised placebo-controlled trial

printed_heading.text: SHORT COMMUNICATION Twelve week liraglutide or sitagliptin does not affect hepatic fat in type 2 diabetes: a randomised placebo-controlled trial Mark M. Smits1 & Lennart Tonneijck1 & Marcel H. A. Muskiet1 & Mark H. H. Kramer1 & Petra J. W. Pouwels2 & Indra C. Pieters-van den Bos3 & Trynke Hoekstra4,5 & Michaela Diamant1 & Daniël H. van Raalte1 & Djuna L. Cahen6 Received: 2 June 2016 /Accepted: 19 August 2016 /Published online: 15 September 2016 # The Author(s) 2016. This article is published with open access at Springerlink.com

what_it_measured.text: We assessed the effects of the GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide and the dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4 inhibitor sitagliptin on hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in patients with type 2 diabetes.

dose.text: Methods In this 12 week, parallel, randomised, placebocontrolled trial, performed at the VU University Medical Center between July 2013 and August 2015, 52 overweight patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and/or sulphonylurea agent ([mean ± SD] age 62.7 ± 6.9 years, HbA1c 7.3 ± 0.7% or 56 ± 1 mmol/mol) were allocated to once daily liraglutide 1.8 mg (n = 17), sitagliptin 100 mg (n = 18) or matching placebos (n = 17) by computer generated numbers.

endpoint.text: Here, the effects of GLP-1-based therapies on the secondary endpoints of hepatic steatosis (measured using proton-magnetic resonance spectroscopy [1H-MRS]), hepatic fibrosis (assessed by fibrosis formulae) and hepatic function (from measurements of serum albumin and bilirubin) are reported.

reported_results.text: At week 12, no between-group differences in hepatic steatosis were found. Liraglutide reduced steatosis by 10% (20.9 ± 3.4% to 18.8 ± 3.3%), sitagliptin reduced steatosis by 12.1% (23.9 ± 3.0% to 21.0 ± 2.7%) and placebo lessened it by 9.5% (18.7 ± 2.7% to 16.9 ± 2.7%). Neither drug affected hepatic fibrosis scores compared with placebo.

numbers.text: Methods In this 12 week, parallel, randomised, placebocontrolled trial, performed at the VU University Medical Center between July 2013 and August 2015, 52 overweight patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and/or sulphonylurea agent ([mean ± SD] age 62.7 ± 6.9 years, HbA1c 7.3 ± 0.7% or 56 ± 1 mmol/mol) were allocated to once daily liraglutide 1.8 mg (n = 17), sitagliptin 100 mg (n = 18) or matching placebos (n = 17) by computer generated numbers.

Here, the effects of GLP-1-based therapies on the secondary endpoints of hepatic steatosis (measured using proton-magnetic resonance spectroscopy [1H-MRS]), hepatic fibrosis (assessed by fibrosis formulae) and hepatic function (from measurements of serum albumin and bilirubin) are reported.

At week 12, no between-group differences in hepatic steatosis were found. Liraglutide reduced steatosis by 10% (20.9 ± 3.4% to 18.8 ± 3.3%), sitagliptin reduced steatosis by 12.1% (23.9 ± 3.0% to 21.0 ± 2.7%) and placebo lessened it by 9.5% (18.7 ± 2.7% to 16.9 ± 2.7%). Neither drug affected hepatic fibrosis scores compared with placebo.
We assessed the effects of the GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide and the dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4 inhibitor sitagliptin on hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in patients with type 2 diabetes.
